newsitem.title: PERU: Lima share prices end up on strong GDP estimates.
newsitem.headline: Lima share prices end up on strong GDP estimates.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange ended with strong gains Friday as investors bought equities hoping the country's strong economic growth potential would translate into solid company profits, brokers said.
With players estimating forthcoming government figures would show April's economic growth as the highest monthly rise this year, prices were also seen climbing Monday, they added.

Friday, the General Index rose 3.83 percent to 2,131.1 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL edged up 3.99 percent to 3,115.7 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
In a total of 3,600 trades, volume was a healthy 63.8 million soles ($24.1 million), brokers said.

"The strong rise was because investors expect a good GDP (gross domestic product) indicator for April," said Julio Alcalde of local brokerage MGS, adding the figure would likely be "very encouraging".

The government is set to publish at the beginning of June statistics for April's GDP growth. Year-on-year growth in the first quarter this year was 4.8 percent, compared with 0.6 percent in the same period of 1996.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru led the market higher, gaining 3.81 percent to close at 6.82 soles on volume of 995,000 shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- rose 3.45 percent to 1.50 soles, on strong volume of 1.1 million shares.
Polymetal miner Milpo gained most in the mining sector's ongoing bull run, climbing 10.0 perecnt to 39.05 soles on volume of 101,000.
